hints: Notice the column obeys Hooke's law, so the compressing force grows from zero to $120 \text{ kN}$ as compression grows to $0.25 \text{ mm}$.
Recall the elastic energy is the area under the $F$-$x$ graph, $E = \frac{1}{2}Fx$, not simply $Fx$.
Convert before multiplying: $120 \text{ kN} = 120000 \text{ N}$ and $0.25 \text{ mm} = 0.00025 \text{ m}$, then check the result is in $\text{J}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: maximum force $F = 120 \text{ kN} = 120000 \text{ N}$ and compression $x = 0.25 \text{ mm} = 2.5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m} = 0.00025 \text{ m}$.
State the rule: for a material obeying Hooke's law, stored elastic energy equals work done, equal to the triangular area under $F$ against $x$, so $E = \frac{1}{2}Fx$.
Substitute with SI units: $E = 0.5 \times 120000 \text{ N} \times 0.00025 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the intermediate product $Fx = 120000 \times 0.00025 = 30 \text{ J}$, then halve it to get $E = 15 \text{ J}$.
Unit check confirms newton-metre equals joule, so $15 \text{ J}$ is sensible and far smaller than kJ values that forget the mm conversion. This is option A.
